profile_text.body:
Modular, founded in 2022 and based in Los Altos, California, describes itself as providing a unified AI inference stack from custom GPU kernels to production cloud serving on NVIDIA and AMD hardware. The company's platform, MAX, is positioned to run AI workloads across diverse hardware including GPUs, CPUs, ASICs, and chips from Trainium, TPU, Qualcomm, Intel, ARM, and Apple. According to its website, the platform supports over 1,000 models including DeepSeek and Kimi out of the box, with the company claiming 2x performance improvements and emphasizing hardware portability and full-stack optimization from kernel to API endpoint.

Modular's approach combines custom GPU kernel optimization with cloud serving capabilities, addressing what it describes as fragmentation in AI infrastructure tooling. The platform supports PyTorch-like model APIs and includes Mojo, a programming language the company presents as relevant to AI development. Leadership includes figures with deep infrastructure backgrounds, including Chris Lattner, who founded and scaled LLVM, Clang, MLIR, Cloud TPUs, and the Swift programming language across roles at Apple, Google, SiFive, and Tesla.

The company operates in California, where it faces 220 law exposure entries according to tracked jurisdictional data.
